claims.title: Reign of Philip II of Macedon
claims.summary: Philip II reformed the Macedonian army and won mastery over the Greek city-states at Chaeronea, laying the foundations for the empire his son Alexander the Great would build across Asia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Macedonia: From the heart of ancient Macedon to a young Balkan republic that had to win the right to its own name.", terralore.co/country/MKD/chronicle#ev-359bce-reign-of-philip-ii-of-macedon, claim TL:MKD:event:359bce:reign-of-philip-ii-of-macedon, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Conquests of Alexander the Great
claims.summary: Alexander III led Macedonian and Greek forces in the conquest of the Persian empire, carrying Hellenistic civilization from Egypt to the Indus before his death at Babylon in 323 BCE.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Macedonia: From the heart of ancient Macedon to a young Balkan republic that had to win the right to its own name.", terralore.co/country/MKD/chronicle#ev-336bce-conquests-of-alexander-the-great, claim TL:MKD:event:336bce:conquests-of-alexander-the-great, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Macedonia becomes a Roman province
claims.summary: After Rome defeated the last Macedonian claimant near Pydna, Macedonia was organised as a Roman province, beginning centuries of Roman and later Byzantine rule over the region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Macedonia: From the heart of ancient Macedon to a young Balkan republic that had to win the right to its own name.", terralore.co/country/MKD/chronicle#ev-148bce-macedonia-becomes-a-roman-province, claim TL:MKD:event:148bce:macedonia-becomes-a-roman-province, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Destruction of Scupi
claims.summary: A devastating earthquake destroyed the Roman city of Scupi near present-day Skopje, an event marking the late-antique decline of the region's classical urban life on the eve of Slavic settlement.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Macedonia: From the heart of ancient Macedon to a young Balkan republic that had to win the right to its own name.", terralore.co/country/MKD/chronicle#ev-518-destruction-of-scupi, claim TL:MKD:event:518:destruction-of-scupi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Slavic settlement of the region
claims.summary: Slavic tribes migrated into the Macedonian interior from the sixth century, transforming the population of the region and laying the basis for its later Slavic-speaking identity.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Macedonia: From the heart of ancient Macedon to a young Balkan republic that had to win the right to its own name.", terralore.co/country/MKD/chronicle#ev-600-slavic-settlement-of-the-region, claim TL:MKD:event:600:slavic-settlement-of-the-region, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Ohrid literary school of Clement and Naum
claims.summary: Saint Clement of Ohrid, with Saint Naum, founded a Slavonic literary school at Ohrid, spreading the Slavic script and Christian learning and making the city a cradle of medieval Slavic culture.

sources.label: Natural and Cultural Heritage of the Ohrid region

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Macedonia: From the heart of ancient Macedon to a young Balkan republic that had to win the right to its own name.", terralore.co/country/MKD/chronicle#ev-886-the-ohrid-literary-school-of-clement-and-naum, claim TL:MKD:event:886:the-ohrid-literary-school-of-clement-and-naum, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tsar Samuel's state centred on Ohrid
claims.summary: Samuel built a powerful western Bulgarian state with its capital and a patriarchate at Ohrid, resisting Byzantine expansion for decades until his defeat by the emperor Basil II.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Macedonia: From the heart of ancient Macedon to a young Balkan republic that had to win the right to its own name.", terralore.co/country/MKD/chronicle#ev-997-tsar-samuel-s-state-centred-on-ohrid, claim TL:MKD:event:997:tsar-samuel-s-state-centred-on-ohrid, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Kleidion and the fall of Samuel
claims.summary: The Byzantine emperor Basil II destroyed Samuel's army at Kleidion; the tsar died shortly afterwards, and by 1018 the region was fully reabsorbed into the Byzantine Empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Macedonia: From the heart of ancient Macedon to a young Balkan republic that had to win the right to its own name.", terralore.co/country/MKD/chronicle#ev-1014-battle-of-kleidion-and-the-fall-of-samuel, claim TL:MKD:event:1014:battle-of-kleidion-and-the-fall-of-samuel, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Archbishopric of Ohrid
claims.summary: After the Byzantine reconquest an autocephalous archbishopric was established at Ohrid, sustaining the city's role as a centre of Orthodox church life and Slavonic learning.

sources.label: Natural and Cultural Heritage of the Ohrid region

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Macedonia: From the heart of ancient Macedon to a young Balkan republic that had to win the right to its own name.", terralore.co/country/MKD/chronicle#ev-1018-the-archbishopric-of-ohrid, claim TL:MKD:event:1018:the-archbishopric-of-ohrid, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ottoman conquest of the region
claims.summary: Ottoman forces conquered Macedonia in the late fourteenth century, beginning roughly five centuries of Ottoman rule during which the region's name lapsed as an administrative term.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Macedonia: From the heart of ancient Macedon to a young Balkan republic that had to win the right to its own name.", terralore.co/country/MKD/chronicle#ev-1371-ottoman-conquest-of-the-region, claim TL:MKD:event:1371:ottoman-conquest-of-the-region, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of IMRO
claims.summary: The Internal Macedonian Revolutionary Organization was founded at Salonika to work for an autonomous Macedonia, its early leaders combining a Macedonian regional with a Bulgarian national identity.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Macedonia: From the heart of ancient Macedon to a young Balkan republic that had to win the right to its own name.", terralore.co/country/MKD/chronicle#ev-1893-founding-of-imro, claim TL:MKD:event:1893:founding-of-imro, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Ilinden Uprising
claims.summary: On St Elijah's Day IMRO launched the Ilinden Uprising against Ottoman rule; though quickly crushed amid severe reprisals, it became a founding event of Macedonian national identity.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Macedonia: From the heart of ancient Macedon to a young Balkan republic that had to win the right to its own name.", terralore.co/country/MKD/chronicle#ev-1903-the-ilinden-uprising, claim TL:MKD:event:1903:the-ilinden-uprising, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Kruševo Republic
claims.summary: During the uprising the insurgents proclaimed a short-lived republic in the town of Kruševo, which the Ottoman army overran after about ten days.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Macedonia: From the heart of ancient Macedon to a young Balkan republic that had to win the right to its own name.", terralore.co/country/MKD/chronicle#ev-1903-the-krusevo-republic, claim TL:MKD:event:1903:the-krusevo-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Balkan Wars and the partition of Macedonia
claims.summary: The Balkan Wars ended Ottoman rule and divided historic Macedonia among Greece, Serbia and Bulgaria; the northern Vardar region passed to Serbia, becoming the core of the future republic.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Macedonia: From the heart of ancient Macedon to a young Balkan republic that had to win the right to its own name.", terralore.co/country/MKD/chronicle#ev-1913-the-balkan-wars-and-the-partition-of-macedonia, claim TL:MKD:event:1913:the-balkan-wars-and-the-partition-of-macedonia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Vardar Macedonia within Yugoslavia
claims.summary: After the First World War the Vardar region was incorporated into the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes (later Yugoslavia), where it was administered as part of Serbia and its Slavic identity discouraged.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Macedonia: From the heart of ancient Macedon to a young Balkan republic that had to win the right to its own name.", terralore.co/country/MKD/chronicle#ev-1918-vardar-macedonia-within-yugoslavia, claim TL:MKD:event:1918:vardar-macedonia-within-yugoslavia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Proclamation of a Macedonian state (ASNOM)
claims.summary: The Anti-Fascist Assembly for the National Liberation of Macedonia met on St Elijah's Day 1944 and proclaimed a Macedonian state within a future Yugoslav federation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Macedonia: From the heart of ancient Macedon to a young Balkan republic that had to win the right to its own name.", terralore.co/country/MKD/chronicle#ev-1944-proclamation-of-a-macedonian-state-asnom, claim TL:MKD:event:1944:proclamation-of-a-macedonian-state-asnom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Socialist Republic of Macedonia and the codified language
claims.summary: A People's (later Socialist) Republic of Macedonia was constituted as one of Yugoslavia's six republics, and a standard Macedonian literary language was codified for the first time.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Macedonia: From the heart of ancient Macedon to a young Balkan republic that had to win the right to its own name.", terralore.co/country/MKD/chronicle#ev-1945-socialist-republic-of-macedonia-and-the, claim TL:MKD:event:1945:socialist-republic-of-macedonia-and-the, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Skopje earthquake
claims.summary: A powerful earthquake devastated Skopje, killing more than a thousand people; the city was rebuilt with international aid as the modern capital of the republic.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of North Macedonia: From the heart of ancient Macedon to a young Balkan republic that had to win the right to its own name.", terralore.co/country/MKD/chronicle#ev-1963-the-skopje-earthquake, claim TL:MKD:event:1963:the-skopje-earthquake, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence referendum
claims.summary: Citizens voted by some 96 percent for independence, and the republic seceded peacefully from Yugoslavia under President Kiro Gligorov, alone among the Yugoslav republics in avoiding war.

claims.title: UN admission as 'FYROM'
claims.summary: Owing to Greece's objection over the name, the country was admitted to the United Nations under the provisional designation 'the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia'.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition: North Macedonia

claims.title: The Interim Accord with Greece
claims.summary: Greece and the country signed an Interim Accord under which Greece agreed not to object to its membership of international bodies referred to by the provisional name.

claims.title: ICJ rules against Greece
claims.summary: The International Court of Justice held that Greece had breached the Interim Accord by objecting to the country's admission to NATO at the 2008 Bucharest summit.

sources.label: Application of the Interim Accord of 13 September 1995 (the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia v. Greece), Judgment of 5 December 2011

claims.title: The Prespa Agreement
claims.summary: Greece and the country signed the Prespa Agreement, renaming it the Republic of North Macedonia (used erga omnes), terminating the 1995 accord and distinguishing the modern Slavic state from ancient Macedon.

sources.label: Prespa Agreement (Final Agreement for the Settlement of the Differences), 17 June 2018

claims.title: The Ohrid Framework Agreement
claims.summary: The agreement ended the 2001 ethnic Albanian insurgency, rejecting territorial partition and granting the Albanian minority greater rights through decentralisation, equitable representation, language rights and double-majority voting.

sources.label: Ohrid Agreement (Framework Agreement, 13 August 2001)

claims.title: EU candidate status
claims.summary: Having applied for membership in 2004, the country was granted European Union candidate status in December 2005, opening a long road toward accession.

claims.title: North Macedonia joins NATO
claims.summary: After the Prespa Agreement lifted Greece's objection, North Macedonia deposited its instrument of accession and became NATO's thirtieth member on 27 March 2020.
